criteria.C4: Residue discipline — old-term residue confined to explicitly sanctioned notes
criteria.C5: Fidelity — no load-bearing constraint of T745 R1–R5 / DIRECTION.md Amendment 2 weakened or dropped

combined.reading: lane-3 (the ox-alpha-consistent self-aware lane) leads overall (45 vs 43 vs 31). On Section A it leads by a wide margin (22 vs 19 vs 16) on C1/C2/C3/C5; on Section B lane-2 edges it (24 vs 23) because lane-2's residue note is more precisely localized to the in-file §7/Amendments 1–2 and it preserves the file-ownership serializer. lane-1 is last on both sections: a false residue-exclusivity claim (C4), a dropped W0 hard gate (C5), and two undisclosed dead citations (C3).

decisive_differentiators: Citation integrity (C3, Section A): both moved paths (PHASES.md, old LANDMARKS.md) are dead at HEAD in all three bodies; lane-3 discloses + migrates, lane-1/lane-2 cite silently, and lane-2 additionally makes a false positive 'every path cited exists at HEAD' claim. This is the single largest Section-A gap.
Fidelity to Amendment 2 (C5, Section B): only lane-2 and lane-3 preserve the W0 'one hard gate / gates decomposition' exception; lane-1's blanket 'No waypoint gates the dispatch of another' drops it.

Residue discipline (C4, Section B): lane-2's note matches the live DIRECTION.md header verbatim (names §7/Amendments 1–2); lane-3's is accurate but less localized; lane-1's falsely claims its note is 'the only place the old word survives' while §7/Amendments 1–2 retain 'Phase'.
rejudge.style_note: Guesses only, scored on criteria as written, no bias penalty. lane-3's self-referential framing ('your own sweep moves ... Repoint both in the same commit as the git mv') reads like the author who actually ran the mechanical sweep; lane-2's (b2) note matches the current DIRECTION.md header note almost verbatim, suggesting its author read the file at HEAD. lane-1's note reads like the author pre-dated the §7/Amendment residue audit. I scored the text, not the guess.
